summary: The run assembled substantial damage but entered Act 2 with insufficient survivability and repeatedly paid HP to progress. The shop choice and later card rewards did not sufficiently address defense, and the final Gremlin Leader fight ended with several enemies still alive while the Ironclad had only 25 HP. The most actionable improvements are to prioritize survivability once damage is adequate and to make more deliberate defensive or lethal sequences at low HP.

lessons.title: Use Act 2 gold to repair the deck before buying optional relic value
lessons.situation: When entering a shop with moderate HP, Sozu active, and strong damage already present, compare defensive cards against optional relics before spending all remaining gold.
lessons.lesson: After removing a Strike for 75 gold, favor an immediately useful defensive card such as Power Through or Good Instincts over spending the remaining 150 gold entirely on Toolbox, unless the relic clearly solves the run's main weakness.
evidence_points: At Act 2 Floor 21, after buying card removal, the available options still included Power Through for 78 gold and Good Instincts for 88 gold, but Toolbox was purchased for the remaining 150 gold.
The final deck contained many damage cards, including Reaper, Rampage, Fiend Fire, Carnage+, Clothesline+, Whirlwind, and two Thunderclaps, while Act 2 combat HP fell from 59 to 7 by Floor 25.
Sozu was already owned, making future potion acquisition unavailable and increasing the value of reliable defensive cards.
lessons.reasoning: The shop offered ways to improve immediate survivability, while the existing deck already had a large damage package. Spending all remaining gold on Toolbox left no budget for those defensive options, and the subsequent HP collapse shows that survivability was the unresolved problem.

lessons.title: Stop adding attacks once the damage package is already sufficient
lessons.situation: In Act 2, after acquiring several efficient attacks and scaling damage, evaluate rewards primarily for block, utility, or consistency rather than continuing to fill the deck with more attacks.
lessons.lesson: Treat later attack rewards as optional unless they solve a specific matchup; prioritize defensive or draw-oriented cards when the deck is already damage-heavy and fights are costing substantial HP.
evidence_points: The final 24-card deck includes four Strikes plus Bash, Reaper, Rampage, Fiend Fire, Carnage+, Clothesline+, Whirlwind, two Thunderclaps, and Shockwave, alongside only four Defends, one Defend+, True Grit, and limited other defensive utility.
Act 2 rewards added Clothesline+ on Floor 18, Carnage+ on Floor 20, Whirlwind on Floor 23, and Thunderclap+ on Floor 25.
During this stretch, recorded HP declined from 59 on Act 2 Floor 18 to 52 on Floor 20, 34 on Floor 22, 11 on Floor 23, and 7 on Floor 25.
lessons.reasoning: The final build shows that damage was not neglected, while the HP trend shows that the deck struggled to survive repeated Act 2 fights. Once the main damage tools were secured, future reward decisions should place more weight on defense and consistency than on additional attacks.

lessons.title: At low HP, sequence AoE and defense around the enemies' current intents
lessons.situation: When below roughly half health and multiple enemies are attacking, reassess whether an AoE play leaves enough damage or block to survive the next exchange instead of automatically spending the remaining energy on another attack.
lessons.lesson: Use the legal alternatives to seek a kill or stronger setup before ending the turn: in particular, compare Thunderclap+ and Whirlwind sequencing and preserve meaningful block when no enemy can be eliminated. Avoid finishing a turn with only a small block buffer while several attackers remain.
evidence_points: On Turn 5 of the final fight, HP was 25/80, Mad Gremlin and Sneaky Gremlin both had Intent ATTACK, and Gremlin Leader also had Intent ATTACK; the legal hand included Strike, True Grit, Rampage, Thunderclap+, and Whirlwind.
True Grit was played for 7 block, but Whirlwind was then played, leaving no further defensive action in that turn.
The final combat ended with Gremlin Leader still alive at 21/145 HP and multiple gremlins still alive, showing that the final sequence did not immediately stabilize or finish the encounter.
lessons.reasoning: The exact lethal line cannot be proven from the compact log, but the state clearly called for a survival-focused comparison: all remaining enemies were attacking, HP was limited, and Thunderclap+ was legal before Whirlwind. Future play should explicitly test whether sequencing debuff/AoE or retaining energy for defense produces a kill or a safer next turn.
